python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Percentage increases from 1942 to 1943
new_haven = 17.3
hartford = 18.6

# First distribution P: (New Haven, Hartford) - normalized
total = new_haven + hartford
P_new_haven = new_haven / total
P_hartford = hartford / total

print(f"P (New Haven): {P_new_haven}")
print(f"P (Hartford): {P_hartford}")

# Second distribution Q: (Hartford, New Haven) - reversed and normalized
# Since we reverse the order, Q gets the values in reversed order
Q_hartford = new_haven / total  # First position gets Hartford's value = New Haven's original
Q_new_haven = hartford / total  # Second position gets New Haven's value = Hartford's original

print(f"Q (New Haven): {Q_new_haven}")
print(f"Q (Hartford): {Q_hartford}")

# Calculate KL divergence: KL(P || Q) = sum(P[i] * log(P[i] / Q[i]))
# For two points: P = [P_new_haven, P_hartford], Q = [Q_new_haven, Q_hartford]

kl_divergence = P_new_haven * math.log(P_new_haven / Q_new_haven) + P_hartford * math.log(P_hartford / Q_hartford)

print(f"\nKL Divergence: {kl_divergence}")
print(f"KL Divergence (5 decimal places): {kl_divergence:.5f}")
EOF
